title: C2LR swap-or-stay lattice
scope: A lattice of trap legs around shared junctions. Each leg supplies one direction bit; the junction waveform is shared by the whole chip.

steps.label: Leg centre
steps.detail: every crystal starts in a named leg

steps.label: Direction bit
steps.detail: toward or away from its paired junction

steps.label: Shared exchange
steps.detail: one matching and one waveform chip-wide

steps.label: Undo shift
steps.detail: every crystal finishes at a leg centre

changes.when: only inside a valid swap-or-stay exchange
changes.reason: The machine's matching deliberately routes two crystals through the shared junction. C1, C2, C4, C6 and C7 check that exception. The general rules return immediately for an ordinary move. R4 and R4d are never removed.

verification: A valid enter–gate–exit tour passes C1–C10 and the standard rules.
Mutations catch a wrong exit (C1), a hand-written route (C2), an unmatched leg (C6), and incomplete wiring metadata (C10).
The checkerboard form is reported as assumed; the demonstrated profile refuses it.

title: WISE switched grid
scope: A grid of cells with switched dynamic electrodes and sample-and-hold shims. Zones are selected first; one shared operation then runs across the selected class.

steps.label: Play one kind
steps.detail: one motion or one gate and angle

changes.reason: W2 requires one parity, while W4 requires one operation kind across the chip. W10 applies the same idea to gates, and W11 requires the shim charge before the layer.

changes.when: only its loop-direction clause on this loop-free grid
changes.reason: There is no named loop direction to compare. R11's junction-pricing clause remains, and W2 plus R4d judge whether the grid motion can be driven.

verification: The generated WISE compiler output passes its complete rule set.
Mutations independently fail mixed parity (W2), mixed gate angles (W10), missing shim charge (W11), and a pair left merged (W1).

title: Cyclone ring codesign
scope: One closed ring of traps. Data stays in balanced partitions while every ancilla advances one trap in lockstep before the next local contacts.

architecture.label: cyclone_base
facts: no junction on the rotation path

steps.label: Ancillas rotate
steps.detail: all advance one trap the same way

changes.reason: Y3 is stricter: the movers must be all ancillas, each moving exactly one trap in the same direction. Y2 separately forbids data movement.
Y4 uses Cyclone's explicit hardware ceiling of 30 ions per trap instead of the standard gate-chain limit of 15.

verification: The Cyclone compiler output passes Y1–Y4 and the deck's selected general rules.
Mutations catch moving data (Y2), leaving an ancilla behind (Y3), a non-ring floorplan (Y1), and capacity 31 (Y4).

title: General conveyor loop
scope: A named closed loop under broadcast wiring. Unlike Cyclone, a conveyor assigns no data/ancilla roles and promises no fixed number of rotations.
source: H2 racetrack architecture and the repository's named-loop control model

architecture.label: h2_racetrack
facts: 40 wells on one closed RF null

steps.label: Shift loaded wells
steps.detail: same signed distance on the loop

steps.label: Dock separately
steps.detail: split or merge in another phase

rule_label: General rules that define a conveyor

changes.reason: No transport rule is suppressed. A valid rigid shift passes all three; counter-rotation or leaving a loaded switchless well behind fails them. Off-loop docks may stay because the rail channel does not drive them.

changes.when: when an ion enters or leaves a dock
changes.reason: The pure rail shift has no split. Docking restores R14: the departing ion must be at the chain end or the programme must pay to reorder it.

verification: A full rigid rotation of h2_racetrack passes the complete standard rule set.
A two-ion counter-rotation fails R4d, R11 and R22 with the conflicting directions in the report.
